title: Cyrus and the Spire
premise: Ulyana Crane poisons herself in small doses for the crown by day and keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things by night, a trade in prophecies, borrowed years, and names that never existed. When her lover Cyrus, a spire-architect's apprentice, appears in a century-old prophecy as the one who will either seal or shatter the Spire that holds an ancient war in suspension, Ulyana realizes the guild has been quietly arranging his whole life as collateral. To save him she must forge the one ledger no one is allowed to alter—the book of prophecy itself—knowing that a forged fate, once read aloud at the Spire, becomes true. In the end Ulyana rewrites the prophecy to name herself in Cyrus's place, seals the war with her own inherited blood, and loses her guild name and immunity forever, while Cyrus chooses love against duty and carries her memory into a world that no longer records either of them.
about_author: Ines Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild registries and now writes fantasy about people who keep dangerous records. She lives near a coastal city of old spires and writes at night, one small poison of a page at a time.

chapters.title: The Taster's Supper
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She tastes the crown's dinner, survives a subtle arsenic attempt, and slips away to the guildhall to balance impossible ledgers. Establishes her double life, her growing immunity, and her quiet love for Cyrus, whom she meets on the roof after. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness cracking into tenderness.

chapters.title: Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Inside the guildhall she records the night's trades: a stolen shadow, a returned name. Her mentor, Guildmaster Ovett, warns her that the Prophecy Ledger—the guild's oldest book—must never be touched by tasters. Emotional beat: belonging shadowed by exclusion; she is trusted with everything except her own history.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Advance
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, ending in Cyrus's. Researching an entry, she finds tonight's date and her own meeting with Cyrus described in a prophecy written a century ago—down to the words he says on the roof. She says nothing to him. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as she realizes his life has been authored.

chapters.title: The Apprentice of the Spire
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He works on repairs to the Spire that crowns the old war-field, where the sealed armies of the Sundering still stand as ash-statues. He notices the Spire humming when Ulyana is near, and his master, Architect Vess, watches him too closely. Emotional beat: ambition and unease; the building seems to know him.

chapters.title: Entries That Erase Themselves
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She tests the Prophecy Ledger and finds later pages blanking out—events unwriting themselves around Cyrus. Ovett catches her and confesses that the guild has been 'stewarding' a prophesied Seal-Bearer for generations, and Cyrus is the current vessel. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that raised her.

chapters.title: What the Guild Bought
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Digging in the deep archive, she learns the guild purchased Cyrus's bloodline a century ago—his great-grandmother traded the family's fate for the guild's protection. Ulyana's own taster post was arranged to build the immunity the prophecy requires. Emotional beat: grief; her whole identity was a line item.

chapters.title: The Poisoner's Court
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At court she detects poison aimed not at the king but at the Spire's visiting Warden, and realizes someone wants the ancient seal broken. She saves the Warden and is noticed—dangerously—for the first time. Emotional beat: duty sharpening into purpose, and into exposure.

chapters.title: Confessions on the Roof
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ulyana tells Cyrus he is prophesied; Cyrus admits the Spire has been speaking to him in his dreams, calling him by a name that isn't his. They vow to defy the guild and the prophecy together. Emotional beat: love as conspiracy; the first honest night either has had.

chapters.title: The Warden's Offer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The Warden reveals the Spire's seal is failing and offers Ulyana a choice: deliver Cyrus to be sealed inside as the prophecy demands, or watch the Sundering armies wake. He shows her the ash-statues stirring. Emotional beat: duty wearing the mask of mercy.

chapters.title: Ovett's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ovett admits the guild has sacrificed a Seal-Bearer every hundred years and offers Ulyana a way out: erase Cyrus's name from every ledger and let an unrecorded man slip fate. But erasure would also erase every memory of him from the world—including hers. Emotional beat: the true price of love made explicit.

chapters.title: The Name That Isn't His
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Following the Spire's dream-voice, Cyrus finds a hidden chamber bearing his face in century-old carvings and learns his 'true' name: the name of the first Seal-Bearer, reborn. He begins to wonder if he is a person or a function. Emotional beat: identity dissolving under inheritance.

chapters.title: Ledger-Burning
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A faction of the guild, led by the taster-master Sef, tries to burn the Prophecy Ledger to free Cyrus by destroying fate itself; the Warden's agents counterattack, and the guildhall burns. Ulyana saves the Ledger and loses Ovett. Emotional beat: rage and loss; the neutral guild takes sides at last.

chapters.title: Fugitives on the War-Field
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ulyana and Cyrus flee across the ash-fields among the stirring statues, hiding in a dead army's trench. They speak plainly about running away, and almost believe it. Emotional beat: stolen peace; the eye of the storm.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Book
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Captured by Sef's faction, Ulyana is forced to read from the Ledger aloud—and discovers the prophecy names a second figure: 'the Taster, who will choose the seal or the sword.' She was always in the book too, hidden in the margins. Emotional beat: horror and strange relief; she was never invisible either.

chapters.title: Vess's Design
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Architect Vess reveals the Spire was built as a lock with one missing piece: a living seal drawn from both bloodlines—Cyrus's and, the prophecy implies, Ulyana's. Vess has spent his life preparing Cyrus for sacrifice and considers it an honor. Emotional beat: duty as a cage built by loving hands.

chapters.title: The Choice in the Margins
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the Ledger's margins Ulyana finds her great-grandmother's hidden notes: a forged prophecy that once redirected fate, proving a written fate can be rewritten—if someone pays the cost in their own name. Emotional beat: hope with a knife in it.

chapters.title: The Spire Opens
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The seal fails at midwinter; the ash-statues wake as the Warden's forces and the guild's survivors converge on the Spire. Cyrus is taken to the sealing chamber. Emotional beat: war igniting, all threads converging.

chapters.title: The Forged Fate
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the chamber, before the assembled powers, Ulyana reads her forged prophecy aloud: the seal will be made not by a sacrificed bearer but by a willing one who gives her name, her immunity, and her recorded self. The Ledger accepts the amendment; the Spire begins to close around her. Emotional beat: terrible resolve; love against duty resolved into love as duty.

chapters.title: Cyrus Refuses
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus breaks from his handlers and refuses the fate written for him, choosing Ulyana over the prophecy—and in choosing, he does the one thing no Seal-Bearer ever has: he says no. The Spire, built to accept consent, wavers. Emotional beat: defiance as the story's thesis made flesh.

chapters.title: The Sealing of the Sundering
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Together they seal the war: Cyrus consents to hold the door from inside the Spire's dream, while Ulyana, nameless and unrecorded, becomes the key that locks it—alive but erased from every ledger, guild, and memory but his. Emotional beat: sacrifice without death; the war ends in a held breath.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Forgot
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The world moves on; the guild rebuilds with a gap in its books no one can explain. Cyrus, freed when the seal stabilized, finds that everyone has forgotten Ulyana except him—and the Spire, which hums her name. Emotional beat: grief and stubborn devotion; memory as the last ledger.

chapters.title: Cyrus and the Spire
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Cyrus becomes the Spire's keeper and writes a new book—unauthorized, uncounted—recording Ulyana's story word by word, and reading it aloud to the stone until, one dawn, the Spire gives her back: unnamed, immune to nothing, real. Emotional beat: resurrection through remembrance; love outlasting fate.
